shared_context.topic: applying ointment to a pierced nipple

snippets.output: Clean the pierced area gently with saline solution or a mild, fragrance-free soap and water. Avoid using alcohol or hydrogen peroxide as they can be too harsh.
snippets.pattern_notes: Cleaning step properties: what to use and what to avoid; parallel guidance on same action.

snippets.output: Dry the area with a clean, soft towel or let it air dry completely.
snippets.pattern_notes: Single atom, same overall topic but distinct checkable step.

snippets.output: Remove the jewelry if possible and if advised by your healthcare provider. This allows for better access to the area and ensures the ointment can be applied directly to the skin.
snippets.pattern_notes: Action plus reasons (allows access, ensures direct application) — causal/justification chain.

snippets.output: Apply a small amount of ointment directly to the pierced area. Use a clean cotton swab or your fingertip to spread the ointment evenly.
snippets.pattern_notes: Two parallel atoms describing the application step: amount and tool.

snippets.output: Reinsert the jewelry if it was removed, ensuring it is clean before doing so.
snippets.pattern_notes: Single atom, distinct step within the same procedure.

snippets.output: Repeat the application as directed by your healthcare provider, typically 2-3 times a day.
If you experience any signs of infection, such as increased redness, swelling, pain, or discharge, contact your healthcare provider promptly.
snippets.pattern_notes: Recommendation plus enumeration of infection signs — properties of the same subject.

snippets.output: When applying ointment to a pierced nipple, wash your hands thoroughly before touching the area to prevent infection.
snippets.pattern_notes: Single atom, distinct hygiene step within the same procedure.
